## One-Day Hands-on Training on Design of UPS Health Monitoring System at IITH

News Date : 13 Dec 2025News ReportOne-Day Hands-on Training on Design of UPS Health Monitoring System at IITHTheB.Tech V Semester students of the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE), Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Technology (MGIT), participated in aone-day hands-on training programon theDesign of a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) Health Monitoring Systemat theIndian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH)on13th December 2025.The training program aimed to providepractical exposure to monitoring critical parameters of UPS systems, ensuring enhancedreliability, efficiency, and operational safety. Students were introduced to thefundamentals of UPS operation, common failure modes, and the significance ofreal-time health monitoringin industrial and power system applications.The hands-on sessions focused onsensor integration, data acquisition, and basic signal processing techniquesfor monitoring key parameters such asvoltage, current, temperature, and battery health. Participants also gained practical experience ininterfacing hardware with microcontrollersandanalyzing system performance.The program significantly strengthened students’ understanding ofpower electronics, embedded systems, and condition monitoring concepts, effectively bridging the gap betweentheoretical knowledge and practical implementation. Overall, the training enhanced students’ technical skills and increased their awareness ofindustrial applications of UPS health monitoring systems.

## One-Day Hands-on Training on Design of UPS Health Monitoring System at IITH

TheB.Tech V Semester students of the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE), Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Technology (MGIT), participated in aone-day hands-on training programon theDesign of a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) Health Monitoring Systemat theIndian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH)on13th December 2025.
The training program aimed to providepractical exposure to monitoring critical parameters of UPS systems, ensuring enhancedreliability, efficiency, and operational safety. Students were introduced to thefundamentals of UPS operation, common failure modes, and the significance ofreal-time health monitoringin industrial and power system applications.
The hands-on sessions focused onsensor integration, data acquisition, and basic signal processing techniquesfor monitoring key parameters such asvoltage, current, temperature, and battery health. Participants also gained practical experience ininterfacing hardware with microcontrollersandanalyzing system performance.
The program significantly strengthened students’ understanding ofpower electronics, embedded systems, and condition monitoring concepts, effectively bridging the gap betweentheoretical knowledge and practical implementation. Overall, the training enhanced students’ technical skills and increased their awareness ofindustrial applications of UPS health monitoring systems.
